title: ID0416026-DC/Si-D/NZ-[Y2 / R5 313059216001] Mainbreaker_QA1 fault
description:
Problem Description: Mainbreaker QA1
Root cause: QA1 auxiliary contact was loose
Solution: Reinsert auxiliary contact properly
Update 3/Apr/2025 - Charger is online but needs understanding what RC did in order to recover the error.

additional_info.body:
Hi Team,
Thanks for looking into this. Based on my experience I believe this is likely the MOE recloser component and not the main switch itself. I have verified that when the QA1 fault occurs there is no ‘normal’ noise/clunking from the charger. I am guessing this is a relatively low cost item and would be the item that is physically moving the switch.
Is there any avenue where we can get a recloser underway to test?
Regards
Neil Soper – Project Engineer
Meridian Energy Limited
M.
+64 21 226 7346

additional_info.subject: RE: [EXTERNAL] RE: ID0416026-DC/Si-D/NZ-[Y2 / R5 313059216001] Mainbreaker_QA1 fault CRM:01811000740
additional_info.body:
Hey Neil,
Thanks for providing this feedback.
The main switch is operated by a motor (Designator MA1 – Part # 3VA9467-0HA20), but the feedback is helpful as maybe it is a signal wiring/timing issue, as sometimes this is successfully closing and other times not.
Have you observed any pattern with the sessions where the main switch is successful or unsuccessful with closing?
Locally, we have not yet had this failure behaviour, so any additional information you have noted would help speed up the process.
This will also help to understand if the fault can be reproduced while doing the site investigation and measure test points.
Hey Ankita,
Could you please review and provide your global insight on this fault?
With Kind Regards,

additional_info.subject: Note to L2
additional_info.body:

After the latest firmware update, the charger was not operational. With the assistance of L3, it has now been updated to firmware version 6.0.3. However, in the customer’s backend, a "mainbreaker issue" is being reported. In the logs, I found an error related to the ELMS heartbeat. There is no available information on this issue, so a child case has been created.
Action Required:
Kindly connect with Sambath and Ferdinand, and also review the child case. Sambath is aware of this issue and has informed Ferdinand, who will be discussing the case with Sambath on Teams.

additional_info.subject: Re: [EXTERNAL] RE: ID0416026-DC/Si-D/NZ-[Y2 / R5 313059216001] Mainbreaker_QA1 fault CRM:01811000740
additional_info.body:
Hello Neil and Liz,
We have done some review of the logs and found that the main breaker fault occurs in the following types:
Main breaker closes successfully and the charger is able to deliver power (as checked on the 31/03)
Main breaker closes slowly, but the feedback signal doesn't show it closed, however power modules are getting power
Main breaker doesn't close at all.
With the Power saving mode and the main breaker switching as needed, this emphasis the issue and risk of it getting a state where it isn't closed.
Based on the number of potential components that all work to close the breaker and requirement to be ready for repair, we will first perform an investigation to identify the faulted component(s).
We have spoken with our available technician and he could arrive on Wednesday (9/04) at 10:30AM.
Would this suit?
After we have identified the parts, we will get the needed parts ready for dispatch and replacement.
With Kind Regards,
Ferdinand Reisch
Siemens Ltd.
Application Service Engineer
Email: ferdinand.reisch@siemens.com
www.siemens.com.au/emobility

additional_info.subject: Note from RC
additional_info.body:
Please see attached the logs for with ("w") the ELMS enabled and the main breaker fault.
Without ("wo") the ELMS enabled and main breaker fault.
And finally from another charger of the same customer without the main breaker fault.
As suggested in the emails, it appears this fault is intermittent with either a slow or non-switching main breaker and a feedback signal which is intermittent.
Initial guess is maybe connection XD31 or XD9.1A being loose.
However we will check the operation of the main breaker QA1, then the signal inputs and also the feedback signal under varied conditions with the charger door closed and remotely monitoring voltage signals.

additional_info.subject: Re: [EXTERNAL] RE: ID0416026-DC/Si-D/NZ-[Y2 / R5 313059216001] Mainbreaker_QA1 fault CRM:01811000740
additional_info.body:
Hello Neil,
Hope you are doing well.
Thank you for your time and help in organising access for Sean to the charger and also the switch board.
After many hours of investigation, we were able to identify and resolve the issue with this charger yesterday, whereby a lose connection to the auxiliary contact of the main breaker was causing inconsistent results.
5/5 Charging sessions progressed successfully into charging from exiting power saving mode, whereby all feedback from the main breaker responded as we expected.
Discussion on topics relating to the session stops and exiting of power saving mode I believe can be continued separately.
If you have any further questions, please do not hesitate to contact me directly, as we will now proceed with closing of this case.
